newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts end down as market gropes for inspiration.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts end down as market gropes for inspiration.

text.p: 1621 GMT -- UK gilts end lower as a lack of fresh data leaves market bereft of inspiration. Dealers say trade will remain thin until Wednesday's auction of 2.5 billion stg of 8.00 percent 2021 gilts provides some impetus.
* March long gilt future settles 10/32 lower at 113.
Treasuries and Bunds also drifted lower and the gilt/Bund spread remained unchanged at 172 basis points in the 10-year area of the curve.
"We've done quite well not to fall more but there's little to get excited about before Wednesday," the salesman said.
Analysts said Wednesday's auction of 2.5 billion stg of 8.0 percent gilts due 2021 should be reasonably well covered.

Demand from investors looking to cover short positions was likely to ensure the auction went smoothly, despite some concern that spreads against Bunds and shorter-dated gilts were not high enough, they said.

"Given the demand I'd expect it to be more than twice covered," said Steve Scott, gilts analyst at Kleinwort Benson Securities. "There are a people out there sitting on short positions and looking to get it back at the auction."
Kevin Adams, gilts analyst at BZW, said a slight cheapening of the stock would be ideal to ensure there was no upset.
"I think it will go off OK, although we might need to see a concession in market levels before we get to it. A bit of steepening would help," Adams said.
Wednesday also sees the start of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's two-day Humphrey Hawkins testimony.

Some analysts said Greenspan could try to inject a note of caution into world markets, as he did in December with a warning about "irrational exuberance" in asset markets which sent bonds and stocks reeling around the globe.

But although dealers said the gilt market would remain nervous ahead of the speech, this caution was not likely to disrupt the auction. "If most of the buying is to fill in shorts, it won't be affected," Scott said.
March short sterling settled two basis points off at 93.72, and June short sterling also settled down two points at 93.56.

Analysts said gilts could benefit again this week from investors switching their funds out of peripheral European markets and into the UK, as doubts grow about whether Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) will take place on time in 1999.

"Gilts will continue to be the beneficiaries of that sort of move," the senior salesman said. "We are advising people to avoid those currencies which are most vulnerable, like the lira, peseta and maybe the French franc, and go for those which are reasonably safe and well-liked like the dollar and sterling."
A survey in Germany's Der Spiegel magazine on Monday said 77 percent of Germans want EMU delayed.
